title: Longest Absolute File Path
description:
A filesystem is encoded as lines separated by newline characters. Each line begins with zero or more tab characters indicating its depth. A name containing a period is a file; other names are directories. Return the length of the longest absolute path to any file, where path components are separated by `/`. Return 0 if there is no file.

## Examples

```text
Input: input = "dir\n\tsubdir1\n\tsubdir2\n\t\tfile.ext"
Output: 20
```

```text
Input: input = "dir\n\tsubdir\n\t\tfile.txt"
Output: 19
```

```text
Input: input = "dir\n\tsubdir"
Output: 0
```

## Constraints

- `1 <= input.length <= 10^4`
- Lines encode a valid filesystem hierarchy: every nested entry has a directory parent.
- Directory names contain letters, digits, and spaces; file names have one period separating a name and extension; both parts contain letters, digits, and spaces.
